chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from some of his men, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
He, who joins to an Imam whose imamate is from Allah another Imam whose imamate is not from Allah, is a polytheist.

key_terms.إمامة: Imamate, the office or authority of the Imam
key_terms.مشركاً: Polytheist, one who associates partners with God

ai.seo_question: What constitutes polytheism (shirk) in relation to the Imams according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Nu'mani’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* clarifies that *shirk* in the context of leadership (*imamah*) occurs when one attributes divine authority to a leader whose appointment is not from Allah, thereby associating them with the true Imam. It underscores the Shia doctrine of *nass* (divine designation), warning that elevating non-divinely appointed figures to the status of infallible guides constitutes a form of polytheism. This criterion is crucial for distinguishing between the Twelve Imams and other religious or political leaders in Shia jurisprudence.

en.abdullah-al-shahin: (8) Muhammad bin Ya’qoob narrated from Muhammad bin Yahya from Muhammad bin al-Husayn from Muhammad bin Sinan from some of his companions that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (as) had said: “
He, who joins to an imam, whose imamate is from Allah, another imam, whose imamate is not from Allah, is a polytheist.”
